subject: Post-call recap: TCO options & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia@fintechscale.com>, Jordan Miles <jmiles@fintechscale.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: TCO options & next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Below is a short recap, the pieces we discussed, and suggested next steps so we all have the same frame for the ROI conversation. I attached a short TCO model (redwood_tco_model_v1.xlsx) and a one-page pricing summary.

Summary of pain points you shared
- Latency spikes during peak batch report generation windows (affects analyst UX).
- Rapid growth forecast: 3M inference requests/month in 6 months.
- Cost sensitivity: Finance has a hard ceiling for initial Q2 spend (~$60k) and wants a clear path to payback.
- Data governance: all PII must stay inside VPC for regulated workflows (we discussed private deployment later).

Goals
- Achieve predictable unit costs under growth scenarios.
- Keep 95th percentile latency under 250ms for interactive routes.
- Pilot with a segment of traffic and measure token economics + caching impact.

High-level token economics (back-of-envelope, see attached workbook for model)
- Current expected usage (from your forecast): ~3M requests/month. Average prompt + response approx 300 tokens/request -> ~900M tokens/month (total tokens).
- Hosted (Redwood API): baseline model cost bucket -> $X per million tokens. For your workload that maps to roughly $Y/month (see sheet).
- Key levers to reduce effective cost: prefix/KV caching, batching, and model quantization. Example conservative assumptions:
  - Prefix/KV caching (repeated context across requests): reduces tokens sent to model by ~40-60% for analyst workflows with shared prompts. Using 50% gives effective tokens ~450M/mo.
  - Batching (concurrent requests handled together): improves throughput and reduces per-token GPU compute, affecting dollar/compute portion by ~20-35% depending on latency SLOs.
  - Quantization & instance selection (int8/4): further reduces cost per token by ~10-25% with minimal quality regression for many tasks.

Scenario examples (see workbook for numbers)
- Conservative hosted scenario (no caching, little batching): ~900M tokens -> approximate hosted spend $XXk/mo.
- Realistic production (50% caching + batching): effective tokens ~450M -> spend roughly 40-60% lower vs conservative, bringing monthly closer to your target range.
- Dedicated/reserved pool: commits lower unit cost by ~30-40% vs on-demand hosted for sustained throughput; amortizes better if you hit the 3M req/mo forecast.

Suggested pilot and next steps
1) 2-week pilot: route 10-15% of traffic (non-critical user group) through Redwood hosted with caching enabled so we can measure real-world cache hit rates and effective token reduction. Deliverables: measured tokens/month, measured 95p latency, and real cost per request.
2) After pilot: review results and model Dedicated reserved pool vs hosted for Q3 commit.
3) Procurement path: if you want us to prepare a draft SOW / PO process, I can loop in our contracts lead.

Attachments: redwood_tco_model_v1.xlsx, redwood_pricing_summary.pdf

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a short version of the pilot plan and a proposed calendar slot for onboarding next week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Thanks Marissa — very helpful summary. A few clarifying items from my side:
1) Finance has carved out $60k for infra in Q2 for this initiative. We need a plan that shows how we stay within that for the pilot and an estimate for ramp to full usage.
2) Latency target: the 95p for interactive routes must be <= 250ms. If caching pushes us to a higher cache-hit % that’s great, but please call out when caching would change UX (e.g., cold-starts).
3) For procurement: please send a draft SOW and an outline of the licensing/commit options.

If you can send the updated numbers with caching assumptions plugged in (conservative and optimistic) by Monday that would help.

—Alicia

Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: TCO options & next steps — updated numbers + pilot plan

Alicia — thanks, I pushed an updated sheet and short summary attached (redwood_tco_model_v1.xlsx, redwood_pricing_summary.pdf). Key numbers below (conservative / optimistic):

Assumptions (from your forecast)
- Traffic: 3M requests/mo
- Avg tokens per full request (prompt + response): 300 tokens

Conservative (low caching, minimal batching)
- Effective tokens/mo: 900M
- Hosted estimate: ~$58k/mo (on-demand pricing assumptions)
- Notes: meets scale but exceeds Q2 budget if run full-tilt.

Realistic (50% cache hit + batching)
- Effective tokens/mo: ~450M
- Hosted estimate: ~$27k/mo
- With moderate batching and int8 quantization, expected platform spend could fall in the $18k–$22k/mo range. This stays well under your $60k Q2 budget even with ramp and extra monitoring/ingress costs.

Dedicated / Reserved pool (12-month commit guidance)
- Reserved unit cost ~30–40% lower than hosted on-demand for sustained throughput. If you commit and achieve predicted volumes, annualized TCO improves materially and shortens payback on implementation.

Pilot plan (2 weeks)
- Scope: route 10–15% of production-like traffic for the analyst workflow.
- Goals: measure cache hit %, tokens per request, 95p latency, and ops complexity.
- Deliverables: measured numbers, cost extrapolation, recommended deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated), and a suggested SOW.
- Requirements from FinTechScale: a small test user cohort and a staging dataset (PII controls scoped) so we can validate cache effectiveness.

Procurement/Contracts
- I attached a draft SOW for the pilot (draft_sow_fintechscale.pdf). If procurement prefers a minimal pilot statement of work, we can tighten it down.

Next step: Can we schedule kick-off on Mon 3/9 or Tue 3/10? If you confirm the cohort and we get staging data access, Dev will stand up the test route and monitoring hooks.

Thanks — looping Dev for the tech sync.

Best,
Marissa
